description: The Khadee Gululem Waterfall, a picturesque cascade, can be found nestled within Sattari, Goa. Sattari, a taluka situated in the North Goa district of India's state of Goa, is characterized by its lush greenery and dense forest cover. Serving as the headquarters for Sattari taluka is the Valpoi municipal council, situated in the north-eastern region of the state. Among the cluster of 14 low-risk waterfalls, the Khadee Gululem Waterfall stands out as an enchanting gem, situated within the confines of the Mhadei Wildlife Sanctuary. This sanctuary, a protected area located in the Western Ghats of South India, holds significance for its rich biodiversity and is even being considered as a potential Project Tiger reserve due to the presence of Bengal tigers. Notably, 11 out of the 14 accessible waterfalls are nestled within the scenic landscapes of Sattari. To ensure the preservation of the sanctuary's pristine environment, visitors to these captivating waterfalls are prohibited from carrying plastic and liquor bottles. Stringent measures are in place, with forest, police, and excise teams stationed at various waterfall sites, including Pali, Hivre, Charwane, Gomdavali, Gulle, Chidambaram, Naneli, Kumthol, Dhadbhaba, Gule, and Khadi Dhadbhaba Gulle, all situated within the boundaries of the Mhadei Wildlife Sanctuary. In essence, the Khadee Gululem Waterfall presents a remarkable opportunity for visitors to immerse themselves in the natural beauty of Sattari, Goa. This captivating cascade, among others, offers a glimpse into the region's awe-inspiring landscapes and is a testament to the area's commitment to responsible tourism. As visitors embark on their journey to this natural wonder within the Mhadei Wildlife Sanctuary, it is imperative to adhere to all designated guidelines and regulations to ensure the protection and longevity of this unique ecological haven.
